annotations.ann_15: cox_log_risk (root: the three identity exits and the four unconnected inputs age, estrec, menostat=Post, tsize -> output 0)

summary: A sparse linear Cox model: the log-risk is an exact sum of three leaf parts and a constant, with 5 direct input edges and four unconnected inputs (age, oestrogen receptor, menopausal status and tumour size; fixing all four changes 0 of 438 training predictions). Hazard ratios per clinical unit, other inputs fixed: tumour_biology gives 1.96 for a grade II and 2.26 for a grade III tumour against grade I, and 0.9984 per fmol/l of progesterone receptor (0.73 per SD); nodal_burden gives 1.051 per positive lymph node, log-linear across the training range; hormone_therapy gives 0.653 for treated patients. Survival performance on the training split: Harrell's C 0.682, Uno's C 0.651, time-dependent AUC at five years 0.707, integrated Brier score 0.132, five-year calibration 50% predicted against 49% observed. Structural and compositional coverage are complete under a single root; the identity-node refactoring preserves the function to 4.4e-16. Every leaf passed its self-probe and grades meaningful on the concept probe: nodal_burden and hormone_therapy are their own input (scores 1.00 and 1.00), while tumour_biology's best single library concept is a progesterone-receptor threshold (score 0.91, R-squared 0.30) that captures its direction and not its value, so that part is described by its three-term formula. Each effect is a time-constant hazard multiplier by construction, not by evidence.

resisted: The resisted list is empty: each of the 5 output terms is a direct input edge, and each leaf's self-probe reproduced its per-unit log-hazard ratio. The limits are of a different kind. tumour_biology, a sum of three terms, has a best single concept that captures direction and not value (score 0.91, R-squared 0.30), so it is described by its formula rather than by one clinical concept. The four unconnected inputs are described as zero-effect (0 of 438 training predictions change when all four are fixed) and not explained, because the evolution left them out; and the hormonal-therapy term is an association learned from this cohort, not a treatment effect. The proportional-hazards form is inherited from the model, not tested.

hazard_ratio_summary: The model multiplies a patient's hazard by 1.96 for a grade II tumour and by 2.26 for a grade III tumour relative to grade I, by 1.051 for each additional positive lymph node, by 0.9984 for each fmol/l of progesterone receptor (0.73 per SD, a protective direction), and by 0.653 when hormonal therapy was given, with the other inputs held fixed; age, oestrogen receptor, menopausal status and tumour size do not enter the log-risk. Across the training patients the log-risk spans a hazard ratio of 5.82 between the 95th- and the 5th-percentile patient, and the five-year risk is read off a Breslow baseline fitted on the training rows.

ph_caveat: The model represents each effect as a time-constant multiplier of the hazard (proportional hazards is inherited from its functional form, not tested), so this explanation is not evidence that any effect is constant over follow-up.
recheck_notes: mismatch 0 and needs_review 0 on both runs (without and with --record report.json); the unchecked free-text sentences are the sentences that state structure, scope or the proportional-hazards caveat without a number. Every write returned text_check errors [] and warnings [] after two fixes made before writing (a typed three-coefficient formula replaced by log_hr_per_sd placeholders; 'zero'/'every' scope words backed by the node-ablation count or reworded). Number audit: get_query was run on all 36 referenced queries; every one is on the train split or a constructed case, and the populations match the scope words (grade cells, therapy cells, pnodes >= 10 / <= 3, the typical patient, the constructed patient at progrec 29.5 and pnodes 3). The hazard-ratio 'spread' percentiles are percentiles of the term's contribution, and the text says so ('between its 95th and 5th percentile'). tumour_biology is honestly partial at the understood level: its best single concept (a progesterone-receptor threshold) carries the direction, not the value, which the hypothesis states.
tool_bugs: (1) query_probe sets/sweeps cannot address one-hot inputs whose names contain '=' (horTh=yes, menostat=Post, tgrade=II, tgrade=III): parse_assign splits at the first '=' and looks up a variable 'horTh' that does not exist. Worked around with hold='where:<cell>' (the subgroup's typical row) plus sets for the continuous inputs, and query_subgroup per cell; menopausal status therefore has no probe sweep and its zero effect rests on the node ablation. (2) query_enumerate refuses the whole model because age has 51 distinct values; there is no way to enumerate only the one-hot subspace. Worked around with one query_subgroup per cell, including the empty both-levels cell. (3) add_evidence strict mode refuses payload fields holding node ids (entry_nodes '-6') as bare numbers; only latex, latex_collapsed and sympy_srepr are exempt, so formula payloads were reduced to those keys. (4) The text checker warned on an AUC quoted at three decimals (auc_with 0.6805 rendered 0.680: 'neither number is the full model's training value'); at four decimals it accepted. (5) The query log of this genome already held a compute_performance query on the test split (q_c3e50aeb46, 138 rows) before my first call; it is not mine and nothing references it. (6) My first pnodes sweep started at 0, outside the training range (the support block said so); it was replaced by a 1-29 sweep and never quoted. (7) An accidental second run of the analytical_formula batch created five duplicate records; there is no remove-evidence tool, so they are amended (reason recorded) as superseded duplicates. (8) get_annotations does not surface the stored meaning block (list_operations does).
